_readme: COPY THIS FILE to config/product.json and fill it in. Never commit the filled copy —
same rule as .env.example. An empty string renders as a visible placeholder rather than
This is the ONE place a product's identity lives. Nothing else in the codebase says the
product's name. Renaming the product is an edit to this file, not a search-and-replace
1. THIS FILE          build-time identity. Name, brand, legal entity. Same in every environment.
2. env vars           runtime wiring. URLs, hosts, keys. Different per environment.
3. tenant-service     per-customer white-label branding. Different per tenant.
Everything under `identifiers` is FROZEN. Read the note inside it before touching it.

identity._help: slug is the lowercase machine name; it appears in file names and CLI output, never in a service name, a table, or a token. legalName is the registered entity exactly as on the commercial registration — leave it empty until incorporation and it will render as a visible placeholder.

urls._help: https only. Any read-only or externally-shared portal MUST be its own origin, never a path on the main app — a separate origin cannot be reached by a flag flip or a routing bug. Optional keys may be omitted entirely; do not leave a broken URL behind.

support._help: securityEmail is required and published for vulnerability disclosure. An auditor, a researcher, and a customer's procurement team will all look for it.

brand._help: Colors live in the token file referenced by tokensRef — never here, and never in code. Paths are relative to the repository root.

locale._help: Every customer-visible string ships in every supported language from day one; bilingual is never bolted on later. `rtl` must be a subset of `supported`. currencyMinorUnits: SAR/USD = 2, KWD/BHD/OMR = 3. Money is stored as an integer in these units — a float loses a minor unit per operation and breaks reconciliation.

legal._help: entityCountry is ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. A Saudi VAT number is 15 digits beginning with 3 — wrong here means wrong on every e-invoice you issue. Leave empty until registered.

_frozen: DO NOT CHANGE THESE WHEN THE PRODUCT IS RENAMED.
They are not cosmetic. They are written into data your customers already hold, and into
artifacts you have already signed. A rebrand that edits one of these is a data-loss event
that no test will catch, because the new value is perfectly well-formed.
jwtIssuer      change it and every live session and refresh token is rejected
linkNs         change it and every share link you have ever sent stops resolving
signatureDomain  change it and every signed artifact fails verification, forever
A signed artifact is immutable. Its signature domain is immutable with it.
TO REBRAND: edit `identity` and `brand`. Leave this block alone.
If one genuinely must change, it is a data migration with a compatibility window — never
a config edit. Versioned identifiers move forward by bumping the version suffix
(`.v1` -> `.v2`); old artifacts keep verifying against the old value. The CI check
enforces this and requires a `MIGRATION:` line in the commit body.

services._help: Internal service names carry NO product name, on purpose. `billing`, never `acme-billing`. A rename must never touch a service name, a database name, a table, a JSON key, a log field, or a header. The schema and the CI check both reject a service name containing the product slug.
